answer: Each new identity must submit a previously unseen answer to a randomly issued prompt, and the ledger rejects any answer already recorded, so replaying an old response fails. For every identity, the attacker must produce a new response carrying a distinct onyx marker and a live pulse timestamp, paying one fresh model run plus one durable storage slot. A separate jade checksum must also differ from every stored checksum, so the answer itself cannot be repeated and mass registration costs scale per identity.
